title: What is UX copy

body.text: every word in the interface: buttons, menus, alerts, placeholders
— these tiny words decide whether the user moves on or gets lost. Claude helps write them clear, short, and human.

example: "A 'OK' button vs 'Save changes' — the latter makes it clear what happens when you tap it, so the user taps with confidence"

title: Principles of good UX copy

body.text: clear (say what the action does) · short (cut unnecessary words) · politely human (not bureaucratic or robotic)
— send the screen to Claude and have it check every message against these principles.

example: "Check the copy on this page: 'The system was unable to process your request' → suggest: 'Couldn't save. Try again.'"

options.text: Every word in the interface, like buttons and alerts

question: Which button is better by UX copy principles?

options.text: 'Save changes', because it clearly states the result
